data.text:
M/S Vantage Biotech Pvt. Ltd vs Drugs Licensing Cum
Controlling ... on 25 June, 2024 
 In The High Court Of Uttarakhand
 At Nainital
 Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Ms. Ritu Bahri
 And
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Rakesh Thapliyal
 25th June, 2024
 Special Appeal No.164 Of 2024
M/s Vantage Biotech Pvt. Ltd. .......Appellant
 Versus
Drugs Licensing cum Controlling Authority and another
 ...Respondents
Counsel for the Appellant : Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel. 
Counsel for State Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder. 
JUDGMENT : 
(per Ms. Ritu Bahri, C.J.) Learned counsel for the appellant has referred to the E-challans, which is at page 46, 47, 48 and 49 of the writ petition, whereby the appellant has deposited the fee for renewal of the drug licence, which was expired in the month of December, 2023. This fee for extended period was deposited on 02.05.2024. 
2. The only objection taken by the respondent/State in the counter affidavit is that this E-challans were not deposited on their portal. 
3. In the impugned order dated 13th May, 2024, Annexure No.5 of the writ petition, it is stated that since the application or the deposit of fees in the prescribed online portal of the Food and Drug Administration Department has not been made within a period prescribed. They are not disputing the fact that this payment has been made on the portal of E-challans before Food Safety and Drug Administration, Uttarakhand, as it is evident from the page 46 of the paper book to the writ petition. 
4. In any case, it is not the case of the respondent/State that the application for renewal was not made within six months of the expiry of the 1st licence. On technical ground, this impugned order Annexure no.5, page 55, to the writ petition, has been passed on 13th May, 2024. 
5. The payment has been made through E- challan is not disputed. 
M/S Vantage Biotech Pvt. Ltd vs Drugs Licensing Cum Controlling ... on 25 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181462528/
1 6. Since the appellant had come up in the present special appeal against the judgment dated 17.05.2024, passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court, where there was no interim order passed. The writ petition is being disposed of on merits. The impugned order dated 13th May, 2024,
Annexure no.5, to the writ petition is being set aside. A direction is being given to the respondents to pass a fresh order after taken into account the payment made through E-challans, at page 46, 47, 48 and 49 of the writ petition, and pass a speaking order. 
7. In view of the above, the special appeal is also disposed of. 
______________ RITU BAHRI, C.J.
___________________ RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
Dt: 25th June, 2024 NR/
